overview: Shelf Availability Early Warning addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in consumer packaged goods operations. The first proof of value uses retailer POS, distributor inventory and store audits. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is out-of-stock store-days, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: retailer POS, distributor inventory and store audits; define out-of-stock store-days and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Commercial Director / Supply Chain VP.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for out-of-stock store-days
